title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #13

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you find first when you read a map? (1 mark)
   A. The colours
   B. The size of the paper
   C. The names of rivers
   D. The north arrow

2. What does the size of a county mean? (1 mark)
   A. The number of people in it
   B. The number of roads in it
   C. The area of land it covers
   D. The number of schools in it

3. Where does a river usually start? (1 mark)
   A. On high land
   B. On the beach
   C. In a lake
   D. In the desert

4. Which is the highest mountain in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Mount Kenya
   B. Mount Elgon
   C. Aberdare Range
   D. Ngong Hills

5. Lake Nakuru is famous for which birds? (1 mark)
   A. Ostriches
   B. Eagles
   C. Flamingos
   D. Owls

6. Which of these is one of the four seasons in the county? (1 mark)
   A. Spring
   B. Autumn
   C. Winter
   D. Rainy season

7. Which symbol on a weather chart shows rain? (1 mark)
   A. A thermometer
   B. A yellow sun
   C. A cloud with lines falling from it
   D. A plain cloud

8. What is weather? (1 mark)
   A. The number of months in a year
   B. How the air is on a particular day
   C. The height of a mountain
   D. The size of a county

9. Which clothing is most suitable in the cold season? (1 mark)
   A. Swimming costumes
   B. Sandals only
   C. Light shorts only
   D. Sweaters and jackets

10. How can a historic place help a county to earn money? (1 mark)
   A. By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   B. By stopping all jobs
   C. By closing to everybody
   D. By selling its walls

11. What should you do when visiting a museum? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   B. Shout loudly
   C. Take objects home
   D. Run around the halls

12. How do religious leaders help the community? (1 mark)
   A. They repair roads
   B. They teach values and comfort people
   C. They drive buses
   D. They sell food

13. What might happen if all drivers stopped working? (1 mark)
   A. Schools would close forever
   B. Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
   C. More crops would grow
   D. Nothing would change

14. Why can no person do every job alone? (1 mark)
   A. People are lazy
   B. Money is not needed
   C. Jobs are not important
   D. There are too many skills and jobs to learn

15. Why is population distribution useful to county planners? (1 mark)
   A. It helps them to change the weather
   B. It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   C. It helps them to grow tea
   D. It helps them to move rivers

16. Why do some herding communities use portable dome-shaped houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are made of concrete
   B. They cannot be moved
   C. They are very tall
   D. They can be moved when the family moves

17. Which of these is a traditional drink of the Kalenjin? (1 mark)
   A. Coffee
   B. Wine
   C. Mursik
   D. Cola

18. On a timeline, which event comes first? (1 mark)
   A. The biggest event
   B. The newest event
   C. The funniest event
   D. The oldest event

19. Which activity involves growing crops and keeping animals? (1 mark)
   A. Mining
   B. Tourism
   C. Fishing
   D. Farming

20. Which of these is a safe way for a child to take part in economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. Carrying heavy loads all day
   B. Helping in the school garden
   C. Working at night
   D. Working in a quarry

21. Which of these is a natural resource? (1 mark)
   A. A tractor
   B. A school building
   C. A road
   D. Water in a river

22. Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of doing what? (1 mark)
   A. Drying fish
   B. Growing tea
   C. Building roads
   D. Cutting down waste

23. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A raw material
   B. A tool
   C. A finished good that is made
   D. A worker

24. Which of these is an honest practice in business? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating customers
   B. Selling bad goods as good
   C. Hiding sales money
   D. Giving correct change

25. Wanjiru sold 10 tomatoes but recorded only 8. What should she do? (1 mark)
   A. Keep quiet
   B. Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   C. Blame a friend
   D. Hide the money

26. Which action shows cooperation? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing tasks in a group
   B. Copying others
   C. Fighting
   D. Doing nothing

27. Which information should you not share with strangers online? (1 mark)
   A. The name of your favourite fruit
   B. A joke
   C. Your home address and password
   D. The weather

28. Who can be a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an elder
   B. Only a president
   C. Only a rich person
   D. Nobody

29. Which of these promotes peace? (1 mark)
   A. Fighting
   B. Sharing
   C. Bullying
   D. Rumours

30. What is child labour? (1 mark)
   A. Doing homework
   B. Light help at home
   C. Playing sports
   D. Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling

31. What should you do if someone makes you feel unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Stay silent
   B. Fight
   C. Keep it a secret
   D. Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult

32. In an election, 12 pupils voted for Amina and 10 for Brian. Who wins? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. Both
   C. Brian
   D. Amina

33. How are members of the Children's Government chosen? (1 mark)
   A. By election
   B. By force
   C. By luck at a market
   D. By buying votes

34. Which item usually comes last on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Opening prayer
   B. Reports
   C. Closing remarks
   D. Reading of minutes

35. Who takes over when the president of the Children's Government is absent? (1 mark)
   A. The cook
   B. The deputy president
   C. The parent
   D. The visitor

36. Which action shows good leadership? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping all the food
   B. Giving only to friends
   C. Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   D. Hiding the food

37. What is a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A market
   C. A large family group with a common ancestor
   D. A kind of road

38. Which quality means treating everyone equally? (1 mark)
   A. Boasting
   B. Fairness
   C. Selfishness
   D. Greed

39. Who is the head of the national government? (1 mark)
   A. The Speaker
   B. The MCA
   C. The Governor
   D. The President

40. Who helps the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The driver
   B. The cook
   C. The pupil
   D. The deputy governor

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why herding communities live in sparsely populated areas. (3 marks)

42. Where can a child go for help if they are being harmed? (2 marks)

43. State three causes of child abuse in a community. (3 marks)

44. Give four instructions to guide a visitor from the school gate to the office using cardinal points. The office is 50 steps north and then 20 steps east of the gate. (4 marks)

45. Explain how a county with a big lake and a dry plain could earn a living from both. (4 marks)

46. Name the three main kinds of historic built environments. (3 marks)

47. Describe how you would prepare for a class visit to a museum, and what you would do during the visit. (5 marks)

48. Who is a clan elder? (2 marks)

49. What is a county assembly? (2 marks)

50. Explain why some cultural practices are no longer kept. (3 marks)

51. Explain what neighbouring counties are. (2 marks)

52. List the steps for solving a conflict peacefully. (4 marks)

53. Explain why children with special needs need extra care and respect. (3 marks)

54. Describe how a class can invite a resource person to talk about leadership. (4 marks)

55. Name the six aspects of traditional culture. (3 marks)

56. Give three examples of artefacts and say how each is used. (3 marks)

57. Give four duties of a religious leader. (4 marks)

58. Explain why traditional culture is important. (3 marks)

59. Give three ways of conserving natural resources. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The north arrow
   Finding north first helps you read all other directions.

2. C — The area of land it covers
   Size means the area of land, not the population.

3. A — On high land
   Rivers start on high land and flow to lower land.

4. A — Mount Kenya
   Mount Kenya is the highest mountain in Kenya.

5. C — Flamingos
   Lake Nakuru is well known for flamingos.

6. D — Rainy season
   The four seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy.

7. C — A cloud with lines falling from it
   Falling lines under a cloud show rain.

8. B — How the air is on a particular day
   Weather describes sun, rain, wind and temperature at a given time.

9. D — Sweaters and jackets
   Warm clothing keeps us comfortable when it is cold.

10. A — By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   Visitors spend money on tickets, guides and crafts.

11. A — Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   Good manners protect the objects and other visitors.

12. B — They teach values and comfort people
   Religious leaders teach good values and care for people.

13. B — Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
   Transport connects producers, shops and hospitals.

14. D — There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   Nobody can grow all food, teach, heal and build alone.

15. B — It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   Services should reach people where they live.

16. D — They can be moved when the family moves
   Portable houses suit families who move with their animals.

17. C — Mursik
   Mursik is fermented milk.

18. D — The oldest event
   Timelines run from oldest to newest.

19. D — Farming
   Farming is growing crops and keeping livestock.

20. B — Helping in the school garden
   Light safe work under supervision is fine.

21. D — Water in a river
   Water in a river is from nature.

22. D — Cutting down waste
   The three Rs cut down waste.

23. C — A finished good that is made
   Products are the goods that come out of a factory.

24. D — Giving correct change
   Honesty is right in business.

25. B — Correct the record and tell the treasurer
   Records must be honest and complete.

26. A — Sharing tasks in a group
   Cooperation is working well with others.

27. C — Your home address and password
   Private details must be kept safe.

28. A — A teacher or an elder
   Ordinary people can be good role models.

29. B — Sharing
   Sharing builds trust and friendship.

30. D — Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   Child labour is harmful and illegal.

31. D — Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   Telling an adult is right.

32. D — Amina
   12 is more than 10.

33. A — By election
   Pupils vote for their leaders.

34. C — Closing remarks
   Meetings end with closing remarks.

35. B — The deputy president
   The deputy helps and takes over.

36. C — Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   Fairness and honesty are good leadership.

37. C — A large family group with a common ancestor
   A clan traces its origin to one ancestor.

38. B — Fairness
   Fair leaders treat all equally.

39. D — The President
   The President leads the national government.

40. D — The deputy governor
   The deputy governor supports the governor.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The land is dry, so it cannot support many farms. Herders move with their animals to look for water and grass. So only a few people stay in one place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: To a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher, or to the child helpline 116.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct source of help.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Poverty, harmful beliefs and lack of knowledge of the law. Accept greed or conflict.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cause.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start at the gate. Walk 50 steps north. Turn to face east. Walk 20 steps east to the office.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear instruction with the right direction.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: People can fish in the lake and sell the fish. People on the dry plain can keep cattle and goats. Both bring food and income. The county can also use both for tourism.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Museums, monuments and cultural centres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct kind.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission from the teacher and the museum, prepare questions, take a notebook, stay with the group, listen to the guide, take notes and do not touch objects.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 5.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: A clan elder is an older respected member of a clan who leads it and keeps its customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for respected older member, 1 mark for leading or keeping customs.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: The county assembly is the group of elected members (MCAs) that makes laws for the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of MCAs, 1 mark for making county laws.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some practices harm people, such as female genital mutilation and early marriage. The law forbids them. We keep the good parts and leave out the harmful ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harm, 1 mark for law, 1 mark for keeping good parts.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neighbouring counties are counties that share a boundary with your county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing a boundary, 1 mark for saying they are next to yours.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stop, calm down, talk and listen, find a solution together, and say sorry and forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step, up to 4.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: They have the same rights as other children. They may be laughed at or neglected. Including them helps them to learn and be happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write a polite invitation, state the topic, give the date and time, and thank the visitor after the talk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, and festivals and ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, 1 mark for two or three.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clay pot for cooking or storing water, a basket for carrying items, and a stool for sitting. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct artefact with use.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lead prayers, teach values, counsel people and visit the sick. Accept conducting weddings or funerals.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives identity, teaches values, and brings people together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees, save water, and reduce waste by reusing and recycling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.
